summary: A playful, essay-style note on giants and titans in world folklore, from Greek Titans and Norse Jotnar to modern games, museum exhibits and poetry. It mixes scholarly quotes with a humorous survival guide for meeting a giant (avoid their path, offer tributes, use wit). It closes by arguing giants live on as metaphors for life's obstacles and as today's industry and technology titans.
one_line: An essay on giants and titans in myth and modern culture, with a humorous survival guide and examples from games, exhibits and poetry.
key_facts: On September 3rd, 2023, historian Dr. Penelope Quinton spoke at the International Folklore Conference in New Haven, saying "Giants and Titans transcend cultural boundaries."
Giants and Titans appear in Greek mythology, Norse sagas, and Native American stories, often representing forces of nature or abstract concepts such as time and space.
The Greek Titans were children of Earth and Sky, locked in an eternal struggle with the Olympian gods.
The Norse Jotnar were creatures of chaos and wild strength, often at odds with the Aesir gods.

On October 12th, Dr. Xavier Thorne presented his "Survival Guide When Encountering Giants and Titans" in a TEDx talk in Rome, advising people to recognize whether a giant is a benevolent Earth giant or a vengeful Titan.
The note's survival guide has three steps: steer clear of their path, give offerings and tributes, and use your wit.
On November 19th, 2023, anthropologist Laura Ingles revealed in her book "Myths Unearthed" that offerings were a common appeasement tactic for giants, such as livestock or barrels of ale.
Mythologist Roberta Collier wrote in a blog article dated January 24th, 2024, that giants and titans are metaphors for the hurdles we face in life.
The game "Titans Among Us" was released on February 14th, 2024; players use stealth, strategy and audacity to survive among giant entities.
The Smithsonian's 'Giants and Titans: Myth in Motion' exhibit opened on March 2nd, 2024, using augmented reality to let visitors feel what it is like to stand in a giant's shadow.
Amanda Jacobs's Pulitzer Prize-winning poetry collection "The Giants' Whisper" is dated April 27th, 2024, and explores human emotions through legendary figures.
The note describes giants of industry and titans of technology as modern embodiments of ancient giants, with mythology written in stock prices and innovation.
